config.demand_profile: 2 hot units @ 200 + 6 warm units @ 50 (total 700 < C=800, 12.5% slack)

headline: Under capacity pressure with shifting demand, AUTOPHAGY (free lowest-utilization units, reallocate to highest-unmet demand) reduces cumulative unmet-demand by 92.9% vs STATIC. Under stationary demand, STATIC remains optimal (autophagy pays a 685-unit thrashing penalty). Benefit is conditional on demand-shift — exactly the dynamical signature autophagy is for. Note: this is a STRUCTURAL rule whose benefit is gated on a DYNAMICAL prerequisite (demand shift). Pure-structural Φ-optimization heuristics in H_312/H_314/H_315 failed; pure-dynamical rules in H_313/H_317 succeeded. AUTOPHAGY survives because it conditions structural reallocation on dynamical signal (utilization observed over time).

anti_tautology_audit.could_autophagy_lose_under_shift: YES — too-aggressive frac would cause thrashing; broken recycling logic would underallocate. Result IS the measurement.
anti_tautology_audit.could_static_lose_under_stationary: YES — if static's d[0] init were wrong-shaped vs the stationary demand, static would accumulate loss. The 0.0 reflects that d[0] equals every-epoch demand under stationary by definition of the regime (not by construction of the policy).
anti_tautology_audit.alloc_eq_demand_by_construction: NO — total capacity is fixed at C=800; redistribution only moves capacity between units; if demand profile sums to > C, unmet > 0 arithmetically.
anti_tautology_audit.win_margin_is_output: YES — 92.9% is computed from measured losses, not preset.
anti_tautology_audit.policy_independence: Both policies run on the SAME deterministic demand stream; no random reseeding between runs.

honest_limits.L1: demand profile is hand-designed (2 hot + 6 warm with periodic rotation); other profiles would yield different margins.
honest_limits.L2: frac=0.30 is one hyperparam choice; lower frac → smaller win, higher frac → thrashing risk. Sweep would refine but not change qualitative result.
honest_limits.L3: loss = unmet-demand only; doesn't penalize over-allocation/wasted capacity. Static auto-balances at d[0]; autophagy benefits from this loss-asymmetry.
honest_limits.L4: 🟢 not 🔵 — measured numbers on a finite simulation, not closed-form identity. Closed-form would require Lyapunov-style argument for the recycling-vs-thrashing tradeoff.

structural_vs_dynamical_placement.pattern_consistency: Consistent with H_316 closure: structural rules survive when they CONDITION on dynamical signals; pure-structural Φ-optimization (greedy local-weakest pick without temporal signal) does NOT transfer.
structural_vs_dynamical_placement.implication_for_anima_M_substrate: M-activation cell-pool could safely use a low-utilization-recycle rule UNDER demand shift (kick-cycle / context switch), but should NOT periodically recycle during stationary conversation — would just thrash.
